## DG4 round 5, code-security review: PASS, with one new Low finding

Candidate `sha256:69b7412a…0e86` (source `3e3a06e`, freeze `e29a735`). I recomputed it in a complete clone and in the repository, at the start and at the end: 1472 files, the same ID each time. I have not read any other reviewer's round-5 record.

**The round-5 repair (T-DG4-FE-R8)** only touches `apps/web`. Nothing under the API, worker, packages or contract changed, and I found no regression.
- **Value RAG lines:** a `not_applicable` line now reads "Not applicable", never "Unknown" and never a number.
- **Business-unit filter:** the browser narrows the unit's list by phase and status the same way the server does (current phase, status, archived excluded) before the 50-transformation limit.
- **Transformation chip:** it is matched against everything the user can read. If nothing remains, no request is sent; it never falls back to "all".

**Does the server still enforce scope on the ids the browser sends?** Yes. I wrote a new probe for the Executive Overview, Finance and adoption dashboards with the business-unit, phase and status filters; it passes 5/5.
- Every id the browser's list offers is accepted, and results stay within the user's scope (63 requests).
- Every forged id list is refused with 404 (120 requests). Ids the user can't read and ids that don't exist get identical 404s, so the response doesn't reveal which records exist.
- ADM-only and outsider callers get 404.

**Earlier probes:** all 14 from rounds 1–4 still pass unchanged, including the authorization sweep (766/766), IDOR checks (204/204), drill-down scope (163/163) and currency (151/151), plus approvals, separation of duties, Finance, gate commit-time and outcome scope.

**Required checks:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint (652 operations), no-CDN, format | all exit 0 |
| Integration, LANG unset (Node 22) | 1975/1975 |
| Integration, LANG=C.UTF-8 (Node 24) | 1975/1975 |
| `validate --historical` DG3, DG2, DG1; `--register DG4`; `--pipeline` | all PASS |
| Unit tests, Node 22 and Node 24 | each has a clean full run (2915/2915, plus 259 with 2 skips) |

The two skipped unit tests are lint-based checks that can't run in that test mode; they pass in the normal mode. Under the load of three parallel reviews, 3 of 5 full unit runs exited 1. In each, the only failure was one session test ("Y1c"); the first Node 22 run also had one known 30 s timeout, which passed when re-run alone.

The commit-time authorization re-check scan, the module graph (`raid` never imports `governance`), worker isolation, decimals, migrations 0028–0061 and the exactly-once suites are all unchanged from round 4 and pass. The live registry, live CI and Keycloak are noted as residuals and pass on their offline checks.

**New finding:**
- **F-DG4-106: Low, not mandatory, not blocking. Owner: frontend-ux-engineer.**
  - **Problem:** test Y1c in `session-bound.test.tsx` requires exactly 2 `GET /me` calls after a create. By design (D-077), the app re-checks identity before any page request sent more than 2 s after the last check. So on a slow machine a third call is correct behaviour, and the required `pnpm test` check fails without any product defect.
  - **Reproduction:** delaying the summary, audit or create response by 2.2 s makes the test fail every time.
  - **Already disclosed before:** in D-118 and in the round-4 domain review.

The review record, findings file and narrative are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG4/round-5/`, and all evidence is under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG4/code-security/round-5/`. The disposable clones have been removed.
